title: 4.10.18.7 Autofill & the language value

labels.name: i18n-tracker
labels.description: Group bringing to attention of Internationalization, or tracked by i18n but not needing response.

body:
The introduction to this section states:

> User agents sometimes have features for helping users fill forms in, **for example prefilling the user's address based on earlier user input**. The autocomplete content attribute can be used to **hint to the user agent** how to, or indeed whether to, provide such a feature.

However, when reviewing the various attribute values, under language it states that the value must be a "...Valid BCP 47 language tag [BCP47]"

This kind of flies in the face of logic. 

The attribute value for any of the autocomplete values is declared in english (the language of HTML) with the intention of being machine-readable - that is how the machine knows to supply a specific value to the input: here the value associated to the user's primary or preferred language, stored as a text string on the user-agent.

Additionally, as I understand the point of this attribute and value, it's to provide "the hint", and not to manipulate or otherwise change the *user-supplied* value of the form input. For the majority of users, the end user will quite likely NOT know the specific language code, and will more likely type in "Francais" (as opposed to "French" or "FR"). I believe there is a confusion here.

Finally, in actual code, where would the language declaration be included? On the form input, or on the form itself?

>  <form lang="fr">
      <label for="foo">Quelle est ta langue maternelle</label>
      <input type="text" autocomplete="language" id="foo">
    </form>

...or the same input, pre-populated:

>  <form lang="fr">
      <label for="foo">Quelle est ta langue maternelle</label>
      <input type="text" autocomplete="language" id="foo" value="Francais">
    </form>

I believe there is a confusion here (while also noting that today, it does not appear that ANY browser is supporting this specific @autocomplete value). However, based on the above, I suspect that the current text as written is incorrect.
